questions.question: If the simple interest on a sum of money at 8% per annum in 2 years is ₹2,000, find the compound interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate in case of annual compounding.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective **Simple Interest** rate for 2 years at 8% = 8 + 8 = 16%.

The effective **Compound Interest** rate for 2 years = 8 + 8 + (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16.64%.

Given that 16% corresponds to ₹2,000.

Required **Compound Interest** (16.64%) = (2000 ÷ 16) × 16.64

⇒ 125 × 16.64 = ₹2080.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹2,000 | **Rate** (R) = 8% p.a. | **Time** (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

CI for 2 years = SI + (Interest on 1st year SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a765e7a3069baa49f8eddd56e6b9f310fd609a10868c22f303a700e081091021.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2000 = (P × 8 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 2000 = 16P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (2000 × 100) ÷ 16

⇒ P = ₹12,500

⇒ SI for 1st year = 2000 ÷ 2 = ₹1000

⇒ **Compound Interest** (CI) = SI for 2 years + (8% of 1st year SI)

⇒ CI = 2000 + (1000 × 8 ÷ 100)

⇒ CI = 2000 + 80 = ₹2080

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of CI

For 2 years, the effective interest rate can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

General CI Formula

Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ, where n is the number of years. CI = A − P.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 12% and 15% on any number of toys bought are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **equivalent single discount** for two successive discounts, use the formula: **a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100**.

Here, a = 12 and b = 15.

Equivalent discount = 12 + 15 − (12 × 15) ÷ 100.

Equivalent discount = 27 − (180 ÷ 100) = 27 − 1.8 = 25.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 12%, Second discount = 15%.

**Formula:** Equivalent Discount % = [1 − (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c9e616056f8255e27fe608c4bdb54576c208991df2c189f7fad8eb0e561aed9.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.

⇒ Price after 12% discount = 100 − 12 = 88.

⇒ Price after 15% discount on 88 = 88 − (15% of 88) = 88 − 13.2 = 74.8.

⇒ Total discount = 100 − 74.8 = 25.2.

⇒ **Single Equivalent Discount %** = (25.2 ÷ 100) × 100 = 25.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When a series of discounts are applied one after another on the **reducing balance**, they are called successive discounts. The total discount is always less than the sum of individual percentages.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price − Discount.</p

questions.question: If 12, 24, 45 and y are in proportion, then the value of y is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For four numbers **a, b, c, d** in proportion, the product of means equals the product of extremes: **a × d = b × c**.

Here, 12 × **y** = 24 × 45.

Dividing by 12: **y** = 2 × 45 = 90.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 12, 24, 45, and **y** are in **proportion**.

**Formula Used:** If a, b, c, d are in proportion, then a/b = c/d.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82c775c1b3e55dace2bbb7d3971358ab5e75e0c0072593c2e520597ad382f6db.png] 

⇒ 12/24 = 45/y

⇒ 1/2 = 45/y

⇒ y = 45 × 2

⇒ y = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in continued proportion (a:b = b:c), then **c** is the third proportional and **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a, b, c, d** are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then **d** is the fourth proportional and **d = (b × c)/a**.</p

questions.question: The natural tendency of objects to resist a change in their state of rest or of uniform motion is called ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Inertia** is the property of an object to resist changes to its state of motion.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in Newton's First Law of Motion, which states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• The concept of inertia was first introduced by Galileo Galilei and later refined by Sir Isaac Newton.
 
• Inertia is directly proportional to the mass of an object; the greater the mass, the greater the inertia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion:** Often called the law of inertia, it states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
 
• **Mass and Inertia:** Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is directly related to the object's inertia. More mass means more inertia.
 
• **Galileo's Contribution:** Galileo's experiments with inclined planes helped in understanding that objects resist changes in their state of motion, laying the groundwork for the concept of inertia.
 
• **Practical Examples:** Common examples of inertia include passengers moving forward in a car when it suddenly stops, or a book remaining at rest on a table until it is pushed.

questions.question: The average of the first 50 natural numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the first **n natural numbers**, the average is always the middle term of the series.

Shortcut Formula: **Average = (n + 1) ÷ 2**

Given **n = 50**, Average = (50 + 1) ÷ 2 = 51 ÷ 2 = 25.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First 50 natural numbers (1, 2, 3, ..., 50).

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Sum of first n natural numbers = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ffa244bf6116b0b5a30e50b9b9040645167e68054941d6978b109678247551e.png] 

⇒ Sum of first 50 numbers = [50 × (50 + 1)] ÷ 2

⇒ Sum = [50 × 51] ÷ 2 = 25 × 51 = 1275

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ n = 1275 ÷ 50

⇒ Average = 25.5

**∴ The correct answer is 25.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any series in AP, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares

Sum of squares of first n natural numbers = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

Average of First n Even Numbers

The average of the first n even natural numbers is always (n + 1).

Average of First n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd natural numbers is exactly n.</p

questions.question: What is the mass number of an atom having 13 protons and 14 neutrons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**27 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mass number of an atom is the sum of its protons and neutrons. In this case, it has 13 protons and 14 neutrons.
 
• The sum of 13 protons and 14 neutrons gives a mass number of 27.
 
• Mass number is represented by the symbol 'A' and is a whole number.
 
• The unit used for mass number is atomic mass unit (u), though it is often just a whole number without units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proton:**

 
 
• A proton is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom.
 
• It has a positive electric charge of +1 elementary charge.
 
• The number of protons in an atom defines the element (e.g., 13 protons define an atom as aluminum).
 
 
 
• **Neutron:**
 
 
• A neutron is a subatomic particle, also found in the nucleus of an atom, with no electric charge.
 
• Neutrons contribute to the atomic mass and stability of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• It determines the chemical properties of an element and its place in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element which differ in neutron number, and consequently in nucleon number.
 
• All isotopes of a given element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in each atom.

questions.question: If x + y = 16 and xy = 48, find the value of x² + y².
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify two numbers whose **sum** is 16 and **product** is 48.

Factors of 48: (12, 4) → 12 + 4 = 16. (True)

Value = 12² + 4² = 144 + 16 = 160.

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + y = 16

xy = 48

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ (16)² = x² + y² + 2 × 48

⇒ 256 = x² + y² + 96

⇒ x² + y² = 256 − 96

⇒ x² + y² = 160

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Squares

The identity (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab can also be used if the difference is known.

Relationship between Identities

(x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy is a common relation used to find the difference between variables.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a solution?

options.text: A solution is a homogenous mixture.
Because of very small particle size, particles do not scatter a beam of light passing through the solution.
The solute particles can be separated from the mixture by the process of filtration.
The particles of a solution are smaller than 1 nm (10⁻⁹ metre) in diameter.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The solute particles can be separated from the mixture by the process of filtration.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A solution is a homogeneous mixture, meaning that its composition is uniform throughout.
 
• Due to the very small size of the particles in a solution (less than 1 nm), they do not scatter light passing through the solution, making it appear clear.
 
• The solute particles in a true solution cannot be separated by filtration because they are too small to be trapped by a filter.
 
• In a solution, the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent, resulting in a single-phase system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures:**

 
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition and appearance throughout.
 
• Examples include saltwater, air, and alloys.
 
 
 
• **Particle Size:**
 
 
• The particles in a true solution are smaller than 1 nm in diameter.
 
• Due to their small size, they cannot be seen with the naked eye.
 
 
 
• **Filtration:**
 
 
• Filtration is a method used to separate solids from liquids or gases using a filter medium that allows the fluid to pass through but retains the solid particles.
 
• It is not effective for separating solute particles in a true solution.
 
 
 
• **Types of Mixtures:**
 
 
• Solutions are a type of homogeneous mixture, where the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent.
 
• Other types of mixtures include colloids and suspensions, which have different particle sizes and properties.

questions.question: Which of the following is the longest part of the alimentary canal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small intestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal, with an average length of about 6-7 meters in adults.
 
• It is divided into three sections: the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
 
• The primary function of the small intestine is the absorption of nutrients and minerals from food.
 
• It has a large surface area due to villi and microvilli, which aid in maximizing nutrient absorption.
 
• The small intestine is crucial for digestion, as it continues the process begun in the stomach and receives bile and pancreatic juices to aid in breaking down food.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Villi and Microvilli**

 
 
• Villi are small, finger-like projections that extend into the lumen of the small intestine.
 
• Microvilli are tiny hair-like structures on the villi that further increase the surface area for absorption.
 
• Both structures significantly enhance the absorption efficiency of the small intestine.
 
 
 
• **Duodenum**
 
 
• The first section of the small intestine, immediately following the stomach.
 
• It receives chyme from the stomach along with bile from the liver and digestive enzymes from the pancreas.
 
 
 
• **Jejunum and Ileum**
 
 
• The jejunum is the middle section of the small intestine, primarily involved in the absorption of nutrients.
 
• The ileum is the final section, which absorbs vitamin B12, bile salts, and any remaining nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Peristalsis**
 
 
• Peristalsis is the series of wave-like muscle contractions that move food through the digestive tract.
 
• In the small intestine, peristalsis helps in mixing the chyme with digestive juices and in pushing it forward for further digestion and absorption.

questions.question: The cost of 2 tables and 3 chairs is Rs. 540, while that of 2 tables and 1 chair is Rs. 470. What is the cost of 2 tables and 2 chairs combinedly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Price** = Price of (2 **Tables** + 3 **Chairs**) − Price of (2 **Tables** + 1 **Chair**)

Price of 2 **Chairs** = ₹540 − ₹470 = ₹70 ⇒ Price of 1 **Chair** = ₹35

Combined cost (2 **Tables** + 2 **Chairs**) = (2 **Tables** + 1 **Chair**) + 1 **Chair**

Total Cost = ₹470 + ₹35 = ₹505

**∴ The correct answer is ₹505.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74bd18c6bc0ab957f4572711ce4b0ed93aa7f7235798e968f6a43bed1eb08ef5.png] 

**Given:**

Cost of 2 **Tables** + 3 **Chairs** = ₹540 ... (i)

Cost of 2 **Tables** + 1 **Chair** = ₹470 ... (ii)

**Calculations:**

Subtracting equation (ii) from (i):

⇒ (2T + 3C) − (2T + 1C) = 540 − 470

⇒ 2 **Chairs** = ₹70

⇒ 1 **Chair** = ₹35

Substituting value of 1 **Chair** in equation (ii):

⇒ 2 **Tables** + 35 = 470

⇒ 2 **Tables** = 470 − 35 = ₹435

Cost of 2 **Tables** + 2 **Chairs**:

⇒ 435 + 2 × 35

⇒ 435 + 70 = ₹505

**∴ The correct answer is ₹505.**

questions.question: If John travels 90 km at a speed of 30 km/h and returns at a speed of 60 km/h, his average speed is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
When the **distance** is constant for two speeds x and y, **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Given x = 30 km/h and y = 60 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 30 × 60) ÷ (30 + 60)

Average Speed = 3600 ÷ 90 = 40 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (one way) = 90 km

Forward speed = 30 km/h

Return speed = 60 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3237db7cfc409000886cb4a2bde76c63b39aa18a65543cf9cd94bf06aeb45cb4.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 90 + 90 = 180 km

⇒ Time 1 (Forward) = Distance ÷ Speed = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 hours

⇒ Time 2 (Return) = Distance ÷ Speed = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 180 ÷ 4.5

⇒ Average Speed = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Harmonic Mean for Average Speed

When distances are equal, average speed is the **Harmonic Mean** of the individual speeds: Avg Speed = 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

If distances d₁, d₂ are covered with speeds v₁, v₂, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂).

Arithmetic Mean Fallacy

Average speed is NOT the simple average (x+y)/2 unless the **time** taken for each segment is identical.</p

questions.question: Rough endoplasmic reticulum looks rough under a microscope because it has particles called _____ attached to its surface.

__
 
• The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is studded with **ribosomes**, which gives it a rough appearance under a microscope.
 
• Ribosomes are essential for **protein synthesis** in the cell.
 
• The RER is primarily involved in the **production and processing of proteins** that are either secreted from the cell, incorporated into the cell's plasma membrane, or used within lysosomes.
 
• Ribosomes are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins** and can be found freely floating in the cytoplasm or attached to the RER.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**

 
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membranes within the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It exists in two forms: **rough ER** (with ribosomes) and **smooth ER** (without ribosomes).
 
• The smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis, metabolism of carbohydrates, and detoxification of drugs and poisons.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis**
 
 
• Protein synthesis is a two-step process: **transcription** and **translation**.
 
• Transcription occurs in the nucleus where DNA is transcribed into mRNA.
 
• Translation occurs at the ribosomes where mRNA is translated into a polypeptide chain, forming proteins.

questions.question: If a 4-digit number 13z4 is divisible by 6, then the greatest possible value of digit ‘z’ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by **6**, it must be divisible by both **2** and **3**.

The number 13z4 is even, so it is divisible by **2**.

For divisibility by **3**, sum of digits 1 + 3 + z + 4 = (8 + z) must be a multiple of 3.

Possible values for z are 1, 4, 7. The **greatest** is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A 4-digit number **13z4** is divisible by **6**.

**Formula Used:** Divisibility rule of 6 = Divisibility by 2 AND Divisibility by 3.

⇒ Divisibility by 2: Last digit is 4 (even), so it is satisfied.

⇒ Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits (1 + 3 + z + 4) = (8 + z).

⇒ (8 + z) must be divisible by 3.

⇒ If z = 1, 8 + 1 = 9 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ If z = 4, 8 + 4 = 12 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ If z = 7, 8 + 7 = 15 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ The values of z are {1, 4, 7}.

⇒ **Greatest value** of z = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 2

A number is divisible by 2 if its **last digit** is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

Composite Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two **co-prime** numbers a and b, then it is divisible by their product (a × b).</p

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper professes to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a false weight and thus gains 25%. For a kg, he uses a weight of:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Gain% = 25% = 1/4 (Ratio of **Profit** to **False Weight**).

Ratio of **True Weight** : **False Weight** = (4+1) : 4 = 5 : 4.

Given **True Weight** (1 kg) = 1000 gm.

5 units = 1000 gm ⇒ 1 unit = 200 gm.

4 units = 4 × 200 = 800 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 800 gm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit percentage = 25%, True weight = 1000 gm.

**Formula:** Gain% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/089660d2d5ccbde72f1c56548bfd83a72ecb32be44c49cd28e0e77b345cc529c.png] 

Let the **False Weight** used be 'x' gm.

⇒ Error = 1000 − x

⇒ 25 = [(1000 − x) ÷ x] × 100

⇒ 25/100 = (1000 − x) ÷ x

⇒ 1/4 = (1000 − x) ÷ x

⇒ x = 4000 − 4x

⇒ 5x = 4000

⇒ x = 800 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 800 gm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

A dealer is dishonest if he claims to sell at **Cost Price** but uses a weight less than the **True Weight**. The profit is always calculated on the weight he actually gives to the customer.

Relationship Formula

Selling Price (Effective) / Cost Price (Effective) = True Weight / False Weight. Use this ratio method for complex problems involving multiple discounts or markups.</p

questions.question: According to one of the laws of refraction, the _______ ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of two transparent media at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Incident**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the law of refraction, the **incident ray**, the refracted ray, and the normal to the interface all lie in the same plane.
 
• This principle is derived from **Snell's Law**, which describes the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction.
 
• The incident ray is the ray that approaches the boundary between two different media, such as air and glass.
 
• The refracted ray is the ray that passes into the second medium and changes direction due to the change in speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snell's Law**

 
 
• Snell's Law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• This law can be mathematically expressed as n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the media.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**
 
 
• The refractive index of a medium is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside the medium compared to vacuum.
 
• It is a dimensionless number defined as n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle**
 
 
• The critical angle is the angle of incidence above which total internal reflection occurs.
 
• It occurs when light travels from a medium with a higher refractive index to one with a lower refractive index.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection**
 
 
• Total internal reflection happens when a ray of light completely reflects back into the original medium, with no refraction occurring.
 
• This phenomenon is utilized in optical fibers and some types of prisms.

questions.question: Iodine is necessary for which gland to make the thyroxine hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thyroid gland**__.

__

• Thyroxine (T4) is the primary hormone produced by the thyroid gland.
 
• Iodine deficiency can lead to hypothyroidism and goiter.
 
• The thyroid gland is located in the neck, below the Adam's apple.
 
• Thyroid hormones regulate the body's metabolic rate, heart and digestive functions, muscle control, brain development, and bone maintenance.

• A condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and depression.
 
 
 
• **Hyperthyroidism:**
 
 
• A condition where the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include weight loss, heat intolerance, increased appetite, and anxiety.
 
 
 
• **Goiter:**
 
 
• An abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• Often caused by iodine deficiency.
 
 
 
• **Iodine:**
 
 
• An essential element required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones.
 
• Found in foods such as seafood, dairy products, grains, and iodized salt.

• Blood tests used to measure levels of T3, T4, and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).

questions.question: sec² A + (cosec² A - 1) - (1 + tan² A) - cot² A = ______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **Trigonometric Identities** directly to simplify the expression.

sec² A + (cosec² A − 1) − (1 + tan² A) − cot² A

Using identities: (1 + tan² A) = sec² A and (cosec² A − 1) = cot² A

⇒ sec² A + cot² A − sec² A − cot² A = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** sec² A + (cosec² A − 1) − (1 + tan² A) − cot² A

**Formula Used:**

1. sec² A − tan² A = 1 ⇒ 1 + tan² A = sec² A

2. cosec² A − cot² A = 1 ⇒ cosec² A − 1 = cot² A

**Calculations:**

⇒ sec² A + (cosec² A − 1) − (1 + tan² A) − cot² A

Substitute (cosec² A − 1) with **cot² A**:

⇒ sec² A + cot² A − (1 + tan² A) − cot² A

The +cot² A and −cot² A cancel each other out:

⇒ sec² A − (1 + tan² A)

Substitute (1 + tan² A) with **sec² A**:

⇒ sec² A − sec² A

⇒ 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Value Substitution Trick

For such identity-based questions, you can substitute a standard angle like A = 45° to quickly verify the numerical result.</p

questions.question: A positive number, when added to its square, gives 56. The number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify two **consecutive integers** whose product is 56, because x + x² = x(x + 1).

Factors of 56 are 7 × 8.

Comparing x(x + 1) = 7 × (7 + 1), we get x = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A **positive number** added to its **square** equals 56.

**Formula Used:** Quadratic Equation x² + bx + c = 0

⇒ Let the number be x.

⇒ x + x² = 56

⇒ x² + x − 56 = 0

⇒ x² + 8x − 7x − 56 = 0

⇒ x(x + 8) − 7(x + 8) = 0

⇒ (x − 7)(x + 8) = 0

⇒ x = 7 or x = −8

⇒ Since the question states it is a **positive number**, x = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines if roots are real or imaginary.

Factorization Method

Splitting the middle term involves finding two numbers that multiply to 'ac' and add up to 'b'.

Consecutive Product Rule

The expression x² + x can always be written as the product of two consecutive integers x(x + 1).</p

questions.question: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon. This property is known as ______

• **Catenation** is the ability of an element to form bonds with other atoms of the same element.
 
• Carbon atoms can form long chains and rings due to their ability to catenate.
 
• This property allows carbon to form a vast number of compounds, more than any other element.
 
• Catenation is a crucial property for the formation of organic molecules, including hydrocarbons and polymers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms, including other carbon atoms.

• **Isomerism:**
 
 
• Carbon compounds can exhibit isomerism, where compounds have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Polymerization:**
 
 
• Carbon compounds can undergo polymerization, where small monomer units join to form large polymers, such as plastics and biological macromolecules.

questions.question: The Earth's crust, metal ores are present in the form of _________

__
 
• Metal ores in the Earth's crust are commonly found in the form of oxides, sulphides, and carbonates.
 
• Oxides include minerals like hematite (Fe₂O₃) and bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O).
 
• Sulphides include minerals such as galena (PbS) and pyrite (FeS₂).
 
• Carbonates include minerals like calcite (CaCO₃) and dolomite (CaMg(CO₃)₂).
 
• These forms are the primary sources for extracting metals in various mining processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxides:** These are compounds of oxygen and metals. They are typically formed through the oxidation process.
 
• **Sulphides:** These are compounds of sulfur with metals. They are generally formed in reducing environments, like hydrothermal vents.
 
• **Carbonates:** These are salts of carbonic acid containing the carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻). They are usually formed in sedimentary environments.
 
• **Mining and Extraction:** The process of obtaining metals from ores involves various techniques like smelting, electrolysis, and chemical reduction.
 
• **Economic Importance:** The extraction of metals from these ores is crucial for various industries including construction, electronics, and manufacturing.

questions.question: In the process of photosynthesis, what happens to the carbohydrates (glucose) that are produced?

options.text: Carbohydrates are stored in the form of glycogen.
All the carbohydrates are immediately used as energy.
All the carbohydrates are stored in the form of a starch.
First, carbohydrates are utilised for energy production and the rest are stored in the form of starch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First, carbohydrates are utilised for energy production and the rest are stored in the form of starch.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbohydrates, primarily glucose, produced during photosynthesis are first utilized by the plant for immediate energy needs.
 
• Plants convert the surplus glucose into starch for storage.
 
• Starch serves as a long-term energy reserve that can be mobilized when the plant requires energy, particularly during times when photosynthesis is not possible (e.g., night or winter).
 
• This storage process ensures that plants have a steady supply of energy to maintain their metabolic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis Process:**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• The general equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
 
 
• **Glucose Utilization:**
 
 
• Glucose can be used immediately in cellular respiration to produce ATP, the energy currency of the cell.
 
• It can also be used to synthesize other organic molecules like cellulose, which is essential for plant cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Starch Storage:**
 
 
• Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units linked together.
 
• It is stored in plastids such as chloroplasts and amyloplasts within plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Energy Metabolism:**
 
 
• During periods of low photosynthetic activity, stored starch is broken down into glucose to meet the energy demands of the plant.
 
• This process ensures that the plant's metabolic functions continue uninterrupted.
 
 
 
• **Additional Storage Forms:**
 
 
• In addition to starch, plants may also store energy in the form of lipids (oils) and proteins in seeds.
 
• These storage forms are crucial for the germination and growth of seedlings.

questions.question: Select the bisexual flower from the provided options.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mustard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mustard is a **bisexual flower**, meaning it has both male (stamens) and female (pistils) reproductive organs in the same flower.
 
• Bisexual flowers are also known as **hermaphroditic flowers**.
 
• In mustard flowers, the stamens and pistils are arranged in such a way that it facilitates **self-pollination and cross-pollination**.
 
• This characteristic of mustard flowers ensures a higher probability of fertilization and seed production.
 
• Mustard plants belong to the family **Brassicaceae**, which includes many other important agricultural crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bisexual Flowers**

 
 
• Bisexual flowers have both stamens (male part) and pistils (female part) in the same flower.
 
• They are capable of both self-pollination and cross-pollination.
 
• Examples include roses, lilies, and tomatoes.
 
 
 
• **Unisexual Flowers**
 
 
• Unisexual flowers have either stamens or pistils, but not both.
 
• They can be either male (staminate) or female (pistillate).
 
• Examples include cucumbers, papayas, and watermelons.
 
 
 
• **Pollination**
 
 
• Pollination is the process of transferring pollen from the male part (anther) to the female part (stigma) of a flower.
 
• It can be mediated by various agents including wind, water, insects, birds, and animals.
 
• Successful pollination leads to fertilization and the production of seeds.
 
 
 
• **Brassicaceae Family**
 
 
• The Brassicaceae family, also known as the mustard family, includes economically important crops such as cabbage, broccoli, and radishes.
 
• Members of this family are known for their distinctive four-petaled flowers arranged in a cross shape.
 
• They are widely cultivated for their nutritional and medicinal values.

questions.question: Which of the following is part of mechanical energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Potential energy** is a form of mechanical energy.
 
• Mechanical energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy in a system.
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its position or state.
 
• Examples of potential energy include gravitational potential energy, elastic potential energy, and chemical potential energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is KE = 0.5 * m * v², where m is mass and v is velocity.
 
• Both potential and kinetic energy are components of mechanical energy.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:**
 
 
• It is the energy possessed by an object due to its position in a gravitational field.
 
• The formula is U = m * g * h, where m is mass, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is height.
 
 
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:**
 
 
• It is the energy stored in elastic materials as the result of their stretching or compressing.
 
• Common examples include springs and rubber bands.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• In a closed system with no external forces, mechanical energy remains constant.
 
• This principle is known as the conservation of mechanical energy.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of metals are found in free state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold and silver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gold** and **silver** are noble metals and are known for their low reactivity, which allows them to be found in their pure, elemental forms in nature.
 
• These metals occur in free state because they do not easily form compounds with other elements due to their low reactivity.
 
• Gold is often found in its native form in quartz veins, alluvial deposits, and other geological environments.
 
• Silver is also found in its native form, frequently in association with gold, and in various mineral ores such as argentite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Native Metals**

 
 
• Native metals are metals found in their pure, metallic form in nature, rather than combined with other elements as compounds.
 
• Examples include gold, silver, platinum, and copper.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series**
 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of elements ordered by their ability to displace other elements in chemical reactions.
 
• Gold and silver are at the bottom of the reactivity series, indicating their low reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Deposits**
 
 
• Alluvial deposits are sediments deposited by rivers and streams, often containing valuable minerals such as gold and silver.
 
• These deposits are a common source of native gold and silver.
 
 
 
• **Gold Mining**
 
 
• Gold mining is the process of extracting gold from the earth, typically from hard rock mining, alluvial deposits, or as a by-product of other mining operations.
 
• Major gold producing countries include China, Australia, and Russia.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms have three-chambered hearts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amphibians, such as frogs, toads, and salamanders, have a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• The three-chambered heart allows for some separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is more efficient than a two-chambered heart.
 
• This heart structure helps amphibians adapt to both aquatic and terrestrial environments.
 
• Amphibians have a double circulation system, where blood passes through the heart twice during each circulation cycle, improving oxygen delivery to tissues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mammals**:

 
 
• Mammals have a four-chambered heart, consisting of two atria and two ventricles, which allows for complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• This separation is essential for maintaining a high metabolic rate and efficient oxygen supply to tissues.
 
 
 
• **Birds**:
 
 
• Birds also possess a four-chambered heart, similar to mammals, facilitating efficient oxygen delivery to support their high-energy demands for flight.
 
• The four-chambered heart ensures a more effective and faster circulation of blood.
 
 
 
• **Fishes**:
 
 
• Fishes have a two-chambered heart, consisting of one atrium and one ventricle, which pumps blood through a single circulation loop.
 
• This system is sufficient for their aquatic lifestyle but less efficient compared to the hearts of amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common application of plaster of Paris?

questions.question: Which of the following elements is extracted by electrolysis reduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sodium (Na)** is extracted by electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• The process is known as the **Downs process**, where molten sodium chloride is electrolyzed.
 
• During electrolysis, sodium ions are reduced at the cathode to form sodium metal.
 
• Sodium is highly reactive and cannot be extracted by simple reduction methods, necessitating the use of electrolysis.
 
• Electrolysis is crucial for extracting highly reactive metals like sodium from their compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis Process**

 
 
• Electrolysis involves passing an electric current through a molten or aqueous solution to cause a chemical change.
 
• It is widely used for extracting metals from their ores and purifying them.
 
• The process is performed in an electrolytic cell, which consists of two electrodes: an anode and a cathode.
 
• During electrolysis, cations move towards the cathode to gain electrons (reduction), and anions move towards the anode to lose electrons (oxidation).
 
 
 
• **Downs Process**
 
 
• This process is specifically used for the extraction of sodium metal from molten sodium chloride.
 
• It involves the use of a carbon anode and an iron cathode in a molten sodium chloride bath.
 
• Sodium is collected at the cathode, while chlorine gas is produced at the anode.
 
• Calcium chloride is often added to lower the melting point of sodium chloride in this process.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series**
 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of elements ordered by their reactivity.
 
• Sodium is placed high in the reactivity series, indicating its high reactivity.
 
• Highly reactive metals like sodium cannot be extracted by simple chemical reduction methods.
 
• Electrolysis is necessary for extracting these metals from their compounds.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sodium**
 
 
• Sodium is used in various industrial processes, including the manufacture of sodium compounds and in the reduction of metals.
 
• It is also used in street lighting and as a heat exchanger in some nuclear reactors.
 
• Sodium compounds, such as sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide, have numerous applications in industries and households.

questions.question: When an object is thrown upward, the force of gravity is _____

options.text: the same as the direction of motion
opposite to the direction of motion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**opposite to the direction of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is thrown upwards, the force of gravity acts downward, opposite to the direction of the object's motion.
 
• The force of gravity is a constant force that always acts towards the center of the Earth.
 
• As the object moves upward, it slows down due to the gravitational pull acting against it.
 
• Once the object reaches its peak height, gravity causes it to accelerate back downwards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravity:**

 
 
• Gravity is a natural phenomenon by which all things with mass or energy are brought towards one another, including objects ranging from atoms and photons to planets and stars.
 
• On Earth, gravity gives weight to physical objects and causes the ocean tides.
 
• It is approximately 9.8 m/s² on the surface of Earth.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• Newton's First Law states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• Newton's Second Law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object times its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• Newton's Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion:**
 
 
• Projectile motion is a form of motion experienced by an object or particle that is thrown near the Earth's surface and moves along a curved path under the action of gravity only.
 
• This curved path was shown by Galileo to be a parabola, but may also be more generally any type of conic section.
 
 
 
• **Peak Height:**
 
 
• The peak height in projectile motion is the highest vertical position along the object's trajectory.
 
• At this point, the vertical component of the velocity is zero.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: In Amoeba, the splitting of the two cells during division can take place in any plane.
Yeast can put out small buds that separate and grow further.
Plasmodium divides into many daughter cells simultaneously by binary fission.
Binary fission occurs in a definite orientation in Leishmania.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodium divides into many daughter cells simultaneously by binary fission.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodium**, the causative agent of malaria, primarily reproduces through a process called **schizogony**, not binary fission.
 
• In schizogony, a single cell divides to form multiple daughter cells, but this is distinct from the process of binary fission.
 
• Binary fission involves the division of a single organism into two parts, each with a copy of the original DNA, which is not the case in Plasmodium.
 
• Plasmodium undergoes multiple fission, forming numerous daughter cells at once, which is a characteristic of its asexual reproduction cycle in the human liver and red blood cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amoeba Reproduction**

 
 
• Amoeba reproduces by binary fission, where the cell splits into two equal halves, and this can occur in any plane.
 
• Each daughter cell is a clone of the parent cell, possessing the same genetic material.
 
 
 
• **Yeast Reproduction**
 
 
• Yeast reproduces asexually by budding, where a small bud forms on the parent cell, grows, and eventually separates to become a new individual.
 
 
 
• **Leishmania Reproduction**
 
 
• Leishmania reproduces by binary fission, which occurs in a specific orientation along the longitudinal axis of the cell.
 
• This process ensures that each daughter cell receives the necessary cellular components to survive and function.
 
 
 
• **Plasmodium Life Cycle**
 
 
• Plasmodium has a complex life cycle involving both asexual (schizogony) and sexual (sporogony) reproduction stages.
 
• In humans, the asexual stage involves schizogony in liver cells and red blood cells, producing merozoites that infect new cells.
 
• The sexual stage occurs in the mosquito vector, leading to the formation of sporozoites, which are transmitted to humans during a mosquito bite.

• Real images are always inverted in concave mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• An image formed by the apparent divergence of light rays from a point.
 
• Virtual images are always erect and cannot be projected onto a screen.

questions.question: The ratio of the radius of the base to the height of a cylinder is 3 : 1. If its volume is 9702 cm³, then the curved surface area of the cylinder is: (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **radius (r)** to **height (h)** = 3 : 1. Let r = 3x and h = x.

Volume = πr²h ⇒ (22/7) × (3x)² × x = 9702.

⇒ (22/7) × 9x³ = 9702 ⇒ x³ = (9702 × 7) ÷ (22 × 9) = 343 ⇒ x = 7.

Radius r = 21 cm, Height h = 7 cm.

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × 7 = 924 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0d1578e8d1be046a9234cd43504e174617eddbc9f9300b63a231892a8482941.png] 

**Given:** Ratio r : h = 3 : 1, Volume (V) = 9702 cm³.

**Formula:** Volume of Cylinder = πr²h; Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh.

⇒ Let r = 3x and h = x.

⇒ (22/7) × (3x)² × x = 9702

⇒ (22/7) × 9x² × x = 9702

⇒ x³ = (9702 × 7) ÷ (22 × 9) = 343

⇒ x = √343 (cube root) = 7

⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm and h = 7 cm

⇒ CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × 7

⇒ CSA = 2 × 22 × 21 = 924 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 924 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Divisibility Shortcut

Since the formula for CSA (2πrh) contains π, the answer must be a multiple of 11. In many exams, only one option satisfies this, helping to identify 924 cm² quickly.</p

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 18 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be one-third filled, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = Efficiency of filling pipe − Efficiency of emptying pipe.

LCM of 12 and 18 is 36 units (Total Capacity).

Filling pipe efficiency = 36 ÷ 12 = 3; Emptying pipe efficiency = 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

Net efficiency = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hour.

Time to fill 1/3rd tank = (1/3 × 36) ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 12 hours, Emptying time = 18 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (hrs)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Filling Pipe 12 36 units +3 
 Emptying Pipe 18 −2 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 3 + (−2) = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 36 units.

⇒ Target volume to be filled = 1/3 × Total capacity = 1/3 × 36 = 12 units.

⇒ Time taken = Target volume ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes add water (positive efficiency), while outlet pipes remove water (negative efficiency). The net work done per hour is the algebraic sum of their efficiencies.

Filling and Emptying Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (y > x), net time to fill the tank is (x × y) ÷ (y − x).

Partial Filling

To find time for a fraction 'k' of the tank, multiply the total time for a full tank by the fraction 'k'.</p

__
 
• **Non-biodegradable substances** do not break down by biological processes and can persist in the environment for a long time.
 
• These substances include plastics, metals, and chemicals that can be harmful to various components of the ecosystem, including plants, animals, and humans.
 
• **Harmful effects** include pollution, toxicity, and disruption of natural processes, which can lead to long-term environmental damage.
 
• Since non-biodegradable substances do not decompose, they accumulate and can cause significant ecological imbalances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pollution**
 
 
• Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances or products into the environment.
 
• It can be categorized into air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution, and noise pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the characteristic of particles of the matter?

options.text: They are very large in size.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are very large in size.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Particles of matter are extremely small** and are beyond the resolution of a standard microscope.
 
• They are in a state of **continuous motion** due to their kinetic energy, which varies with temperature.
 
• There is always **space between particles** of matter, which is evident from the diffusion of gases and mixing of liquids.
 
• Particles of matter **attract each other** with forces that vary depending on the type of matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brownian Motion:**

 
 
• It is the random movement of particles suspended in a fluid, resulting from their collision with quick atoms or molecules in the gas or liquid.
 
• This phenomenon supports the theory that particles are in continuous motion.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion:**
 
 
• It is the process by which particles spread from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
 
• Diffusion demonstrates that particles have space between them and are constantly moving.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:**
 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion which act between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Examples include hydrogen bonds, Van der Waals forces, and ionic bonds.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Matter:**
 
 
• This theory states that matter is composed of a large number of small particles that are in constant motion.
 
• The temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by Leishmania?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kala-azar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kala-azar**, also known as visceral leishmaniasis, is caused by the protozoan parasite **Leishmania donovani**.
 
• The disease is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female **phlebotomine sandflies**.
 
• **Symptoms** of Kala-azar include prolonged fever, weight loss, enlargement of the spleen and liver, and anemia.
 
• It primarily affects people in **tropical and subtropical regions**, including countries like India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Brazil, and Sudan.
 
• Without treatment, Kala-azar can be fatal, but it is treatable with antileishmanial drugs such as **Amphotericin B** and **Miltefosine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leishmaniasis**

 
 
• Leishmaniasis is a disease caused by infection with Leishmania parasites, which are spread by the bite of infected sandflies.
 
• There are three main forms of leishmaniasis: visceral (Kala-azar), cutaneous, and mucocutaneous.
 
• Cutaneous leishmaniasis causes skin sores, while mucocutaneous leishmaniasis can lead to ulcers in the mouth, nose, and throat.
 
 
 
• **Phlebotomine Sandflies**
 
 
• These are the vectors responsible for transmitting Leishmania parasites to humans.
 
• They are tiny, about one-third the size of mosquitoes, and are typically active during dusk and dawn.
 
 
 
• **Diagnosis and Treatment**
 
 
• Diagnosis of Kala-azar often involves serological tests, bone marrow or spleen aspiration, and PCR testing.
 
• Treatment includes antileishmanial medications such as Amphotericin B, Miltefosine, and Sodium Stibogluconate.
 
 
 
• **Prevention**
 
 
• Preventive measures include vector control through insecticide spraying, use of bed nets, and reducing exposure to sandfly bites.
 
• Education and awareness campaigns are crucial in endemic areas to prevent the spread of the disease.

questions.question: The ratio between volume of a sphere and volume of a circumscribing right circular cylinder is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **sphere** circumscribed by a **cylinder**, the height of the cylinder **h = 2r** and the radius is the same **r**.

Volume ratio = (4/3)πr³ : πr²(2r)

Volume ratio = (4/3) : 2 = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32e8f52eb257f42addce73c78a6ca85bf8f7e4ded4a464b8fa764403a9db112e.png] 

**Given:**

A **sphere** is perfectly enclosed (circumscribed) by a **right circular cylinder**.

Radius of sphere = **r**

Radius of cylinder = **r**

Height of cylinder (h) = Diameter of sphere = **2r**

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere (Vₛ) = (4/3)πr³

Volume of Cylinder (V꜀) = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Vₛ : V꜀ = [(4/3)πr³] : [πr² × (2r)]

⇒ Vₛ : V꜀ = [(4/3)πr³] : [2πr³]

⇒ Ratio = (4/3) : 2

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 6

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Archimedes' Discovery

Archimedes proved that both the **volume** and **surface area** of a sphere are 2/3 of the circumscribing cylinder.

Surface Area Ratio

The ratio of the surface area of a sphere to the **total surface area** of a circumscribing cylinder is 4πr² : 6πr² = 2 : 3.

Curved Surface Area Ratio

The surface area of the sphere is exactly equal to the **curved surface area** of the cylinder (4πr² : 2πr(2r) = 1 : 1).</p

questions.question: A and B working alone can do a work in 40 days and 30 days, respectively. They started the work together, but B left after some time and A finished the remaining work in 5 days. How many days after starting did B leave the work?

Work done by **A** and **B** together = 120 − 15 = 105 units.

Number of days **B** worked = 105 ÷ (3 + 4) = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 days.

questions.question: The pH value of the neutral solution is __________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A neutral solution has a pH value of **7**.
 
• The pH scale ranges from **0 to 14**, with 7 being neutral.
 
• Pure water, which is a neutral solution, has a pH value of **7** at 25°C.
 
• A pH value less than 7 indicates an acidic solution, while a pH value greater than 7 indicates a basic solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **pH Scale**

 
 
• The pH scale measures the acidity or basicity of a solution.
 
• It is a logarithmic scale, meaning each whole number change represents a tenfold change in acidity/basicity.
 
• A pH value of 7 is considered neutral, values below 7 are acidic, and values above 7 are basic or alkaline.
 
 
 
• **Acids and Bases**
 
 
• Acids have a pH less than 7 and release hydrogen ions (H⁺) in solution.
 
• Bases have a pH greater than 7 and release hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in solution.
 
• Common examples include hydrochloric acid (HCl) for acids and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) for bases.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization**
 
 
• Neutralization is a chemical reaction between an acid and a base, producing water and a salt.
 
• This reaction can help bring the pH of a solution closer to 7.
 
• The general form of the reaction is: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.
 
 
 
• **Importance of pH**
 
 
• pH is crucial in various fields including chemistry, biology, medicine, agriculture, and environmental science.
 
• Many biological processes are pH-dependent, such as enzyme activity and cellular metabolism.
 
• Soil pH affects plant growth and nutrient availability.

questions.question: If the angles (5x - 2)° and 82° form a pair of supplementary angles, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **supplementary angles**, the sum is always 180°.

(5x − 2) + 82 = 180

5x + 80 = 180

5x = 100

x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First angle = (5x − 2)°

Second angle = 82°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of **supplementary angles** = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/141a9a0abc05d2f14b979755015e2e339138aed03b6d2c270d15a5d4077c368a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (5x − 2) + 82 = 180

⇒ 5x + 80 = 180

⇒ 5x = 180 − 80

⇒ 5x = 100

⇒ x = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary when their measures add up to 180 degrees. They form a linear pair if they are adjacent.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if the sum of their measures is exactly 90 degrees.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then the angles are supplementary, meaning they lie on a straight line.</p

questions.question: A body is thrown up and it reaches a height of 5m and then falls down, the total displacement and the total distance covered by the body respectively would be:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement vs Distance**

 
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity with both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Distance** is a scalar quantity and only considers the magnitude.

• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.

• **Projectile Motion**

questions.question: Express 0.overline{52} in the form (p)/(q) where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **pure recurring decimal** (where the repetition starts immediately after the decimal point):

**Numerator** = The repeating number itself = 52

**Denominator** = Write 9 for each digit that is repeating. Since 5 and 2 (two digits) are repeating, we write 99.

Fraction = 52/99

**∴ The correct answer is 52/99.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A recurring decimal 0.525252...

**Method:** Algebraic substitution and subtraction to eliminate the recurring part.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/739e11e963ff8b9729f8c04b0a53ae367bff34a163503fe87d13ca3a9b151e96.png] 
⇒ Let x = 0.525252... — (i)
⇒ Since two digits are repeating, multiply both sides by 10² = 100:
⇒ 100x = 52.525252... — (ii)
⇒ Subtracting equation (i) from equation (ii):
⇒ 100x − x = 52.525252... − 0.525252...
⇒ 99x = 52
⇒ x = 52/99

**∴ The correct answer is 52/99.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pure Recurring Decimal

A decimal in which all digits after the decimal point repeat. To convert, use the repeating digits as the **numerator** and an equal number of 9s as the **denominator**.

Mixed Recurring Decimal

A decimal where some digits repeat and some do not (e.g., 0.1222...). Rule: (Full number − Non-repeating part) ÷ (9 for each repeating digit followed by 0 for each non-repeating digit).

Rational Numbers

Any number that can be written as **p/q** where **q ≠ 0**. Every terminating or recurring decimal is a **rational number**.

Simplification Rule

Always check if the resulting fraction p/q can be simplified further by dividing both numerator and denominator by their **HCF**. In 52/99, the HCF is 1, so it is in simplest form.</p

questions.question: In the set {61, 62...100}, the sum of the second greatest and the second smallest prime numbers is:

**Given:** Set of numbers from **61 to 100**.

**Step 3:** Identify the **second greatest prime** number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers (1-100)

There are exactly **25 prime numbers** between 1 and 100. A prime number has only two factors: 1 and itself.

Divisibility Rule for Primes

To check if a number **n** is prime, test divisibility by primes up to **√n**. For numbers up to 100, check divisibility by 2, 3, 5, and 7.

Consecutive Primes

2 and 3 are the only **consecutive natural numbers** that are both prime. All other primes (except 2) are odd.</p

questions.question: Which of the following parts of a plant does NOT take part in vegetative propagation?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Flowers** are the reproductive parts of a plant and are primarily involved in sexual reproduction.
 
• Vegetative propagation occurs through parts of the plant such as roots, stems, and leaves, but not through flowers.
 
• Common methods of vegetative propagation include cutting, grafting, layering, and tissue culture.
 
• Examples of vegetative propagation include the use of potato tubers (stems), sweet potato (roots), and Bryophyllum leaves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It allows for the rapid multiplication of plants and ensures genetic uniformity of the offspring.
 
• This method is widely used in horticulture and agriculture for the propagation of plants like sugarcane, banana, and grapes.
 
 
 
• **Sexual Reproduction in Plants**
 
 
• Involves the fusion of male and female gametes resulting in the formation of seeds and fruit.
 
• Flowers are the reproductive organs that contain the male (stamens) and female (pistils) reproductive structures.
 
• Pollination and fertilization are key processes in sexual reproduction in plants.
 
 
 
• **Grafting**
 
 
• A horticultural technique where tissues from one plant are inserted into those of another so that the two sets of vascular tissues may join together.
 
• Commonly used for the propagation of fruit trees and roses.
 
 
 
• **Tissue Culture**
 
 
• A technique used to grow plants under sterile conditions on a nutrient culture medium.
 
• It is used for the propagation of plants like orchids and for the conservation of rare and endangered species.

questions.question: A is twice as old as B. B is (1)/(3) as old as C. The sum of ages of A. B and C is 42 years, find the sum of the ages of A and B.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Let the age of **B** be 1 unit.

Ratio of ages **A : B : C** = 2 : 1 : 3.

Total ratio units = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 units → 42 years.

1 unit = 7 years.

Sum of **A and B** = 2 + 1 = 3 units = 3 × 7 = 21 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfa3d077f097127143d177a06c84634317e5c006862c2655009dece4ac55065e.png] 
**Given:**

Age of **A** = 2 × Age of **B**

Age of **B** = 1/3 × Age of **C** ⇒ Age of **C** = 3 × Age of **B**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let age of **B** = x years

⇒ Age of **A** = 2x and Age of **C** = 3x

⇒ 2x + x + 3x = 42

⇒ 6x = 42

⇒ x = 7 years

⇒ Sum of **A and B** = 2x + x = 3x

⇒ Sum = 3 × 7 = 21 years

**∴ The correct answer is 21 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion in Ages

When ages are given in multiples or fractions, express all individuals in terms of a single variable to simplify the linear equation.

Age Difference Property

The difference between the ages of two persons remains constant regardless of the number of years passed or preceding.</p

questions.question: Consider a ray passing through the principal focus and not parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror, after reflection, it will:

options.text: emerge parallel to the principal axis
pass through the centre of curvature
emerge obliquely to the principal axis

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**emerge parallel to the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A concave mirror follows the laws of reflection, where the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• When a ray passes through the principal focus of a concave mirror, it is reflected such that it travels parallel to the principal axis.
 
• The principal focus is the point where parallel rays converge after reflection.
 
• This property is used in various optical instruments like telescopes and headlights of vehicles to direct light beams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward.
 
• It converges light rays to a focal point.
 
• Commonly used in applications requiring light convergence like solar cookers and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Principal Focus**
 
 
• The point on the principal axis where light rays parallel to the axis converge after reflection.
 
• It is a characteristic point for concave mirrors and is located halfway between the mirror’s surface and the center of curvature.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature**
 
 
• The center of the sphere from which the concave mirror segment is cut.
 
• It lies on the principal axis of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis**
 
 
• The line passing through the center of curvature and the midpoint of the mirror.
 
• It serves as the reference line for measuring angles of incidence and reflection.
